brief.headline: Memory pricing spikes 58-75% QoQ in Q2; SK Hynix widens lead on Samsung strike risk and HBM4 lag
brief.summary: <cite index="17-1,14-1">DRAM contract prices rose 58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026 following Q1's record 90-95% surge, while NAND jumped 70-75%.</cite> <cite index="24-10,27-5">Hyperscaler capex hit $725 billion in 2026, nearly double 2025 estimates, with sustained AI infrastructure demand absorbing all available supply.</cite> <cite index="41-1,41-4">JPMorgan raised Samsung to ₩480k and SK Hynix to ₩3m this morning, citing structural growth and LTA frameworks reshaping memory valuations.</cite> <cite index="47-1,49-4">SK Hynix surged 7.68% to approach ₩2m while Samsung lags on strike risk: 50,000-worker walkout starts May 21, threatening 3-4% of global DRAM supply.</cite> <cite index="49-4,49-6">Samsung began HBM4 mass shipments in February, but SK Hynix has made no comparable announcement and targets HBM4E for 2027.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: Long SK Hynix / Short Samsung. <cite index="3-10,9-8">SK Hynix holds 70% HBM4 share for Nvidia Rubin and 57% overall HBM market versus Samsung's 35%.</cite> <cite index="49-9,50-4">JPMorgan estimates Samsung's 18-day strike could cut annual operating profit by >₩40tr and disrupt 3-4% of global DRAM.</cite> <cite index="50-5,50-15">~200 Samsung engineers defected to SK Hynix after SK's 10% operating-profit sharing deal, averaging $100k bonuses.</cite> <cite index="42-1,43-22">Today's price action confirms divergence: SK Hynix +1.15% to ₩1.836m while Samsung +3.88% rebound is fragile given strike headlines dominate flow.</cite> Strike-free execution, HBM leadership, and FCF visibility vs. labor disruption, HBM4 timing questions, and chaebol governance overhang make this the cleanest relative value setup in memory.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="17-1,17-19">Q2 2026 DRAM +58-63% QoQ (following Q1's record +90-95%), NAND +70-75%; rates decelerating but from extraordinary base.</cite> <cite index="17-6,17-7">Producers prioritize HBM over conventional DRAM; every quarter without new capacity locks in higher prices for next cycle.</cite> <cite index="17-13,17-17">No credible relief before 2H 2027; new fab capacity won't reach volume before late 2027 or 2028.</cite> <cite index="15-22,27-1">Hyperscaler capex $725bn in 2026 vs. $365bn estimated one year ago—demand curve structurally above supply.</cite> Structural, not cyclical.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="1-1">Samsung and SK Hynix raised HBM3E prices ~20% for 2026 deliveries following Nvidia H200 China approval.</cite> <cite index="3-4,3-5">SK Hynix holds 62% HBM shipment share (Q2 2025) and 57% revenue share (Q3); Goldman/UBS expect >50% share maintained through 2026.</cite> <cite index="9-1,9-8">Morgan Stanley reversed HBM3E decline forecast due to China H200 demand adding ~$3bn incremental, citing tightness into 2026.</cite> <cite index="4-1">Goldman Sachs notes Samsung's HBM3E is priced 5% below SK Hynix, but expects 28% YoY decline to $10/GB under competitive pressure offset by HBM4's 40% premium.</cite> <cite index="34-14,40-3">NVIDIA locked >60% of TSMC CoWoS capacity through 2027, creating fierce bidding war for remaining slots.</cite> <cite index="49-6,49-10">Samsung began HBM4 mass shipments (Feb 2026) but SK Hynix targets HBM4E for 2027; Samsung holds ~40% DRAM share but only 35% HBM vs. SK's 57%.</cite>

news_pulse.headline: JPMorgan raises Samsung to ₩480k, SK Hynix to ₩3m on structural growth, LTA framework shift
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="41-4,41-10">Memory enters structural growth phase driven by AI; LTAs between CSPs and suppliers reduce volatility, shifting valuation from PBR (cyclical) to PE (growth) framework.</cite> <cite index="41-6,41-7">Samsung EPS lifted 1-5% on DRAM/NAND/HBM upward revisions; SK Hynix EPS +9-20% for 2026-28.</cite>

news_pulse.headline: DRAM +58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026, NAND +70-75%; Q1 saw record 90-95% DRAM surge
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="17-1,17-11">Contract pricing acceleration decelerating from Q1 but still extreme; NAND now outpaces DRAM for first time in cycle.</cite> <cite index="17-12,17-13">AI infrastructure sold out 2026; no relief before 2H 2027 as fab capacity lags.</cite> Spot shortages worse than contract data suggests.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler capex $725bn in 2026, up from $365bn estimate one year ago; 2027 seen >$1tr
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="27-1,27-8">2026 capex nearly doubled vs. mid-2025 consensus; Microsoft/Amazon/Alphabet/Meta each raised guidance in Q1 earnings.</cite> <cite index="28-1,28-3">2027 capex now forecast >$1tr by Evercore/BofA.</cite> <cite index="15-22">Top-8 CSPs projected $600bn+ in 2026, 40% YoY increase; majority directed at GPUs/accelerators consuming HBM at 3:1 ratio vs. DDR5.</cite>

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity hits 120-130k wpm by end-2026, up from 35k in late 2024; still sold out
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="32-5,32-6">~10x expansion from end-2023 driven by Nvidia B200/GB200 and AMD MI300X/MI400 demand.</cite> <cite index="36-7,38-2">TSMC CEO C.C. Wei confirms CoWoS extremely tight and sold out through 2026; oversubscribed through at least mid-2026.</cite> <cite index="34-14">Nvidia secured >60% of total CoWoS for 2025-26.</cite> Packaging, not HBM, is binding constraint for high-end AI chips.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung 50k-worker strike starts May 21 for 18 days; union targets ₩40-45tr profit-sharing pool
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="49-9,50-4">JPMorgan estimates strike could cut Samsung annual operating profit >₩40tr; TrendForce sees 3-4% global DRAM and 2-3% NAND capacity at risk.</cite> <cite index="49-7">Single half-day rally in April cut daily memory output 18.4%, foundry 58%.</cite> <cite index="49-10,49-11">Samsung ships HBM4 for Nvidia Rubin; any delivery interruption risks hyperscaler defection to SK Hynix (57% HBM share).</cite>

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix approaches ₩2m, up 7.68%; Samsung lags at +1.79% on strike fears
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="47-1,47-7">SK Hynix hit all-time high ₩1.976m on May 13, briefly touched ₩1.999m in after-hours; Samsung closed ₩284k, below prior session and intraday highs.</cite> <cite index="47-16,47-17">18-day strike from May 21-June 7 risks customer defections amid semiconductor boom; 8 days remain for dialogue.</cite> Relative performance validates pair trade thesis.

news_pulse.headline: ~200 Samsung engineers defected to SK Hynix since December on $100k avg bonus vs. dispute
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="50-5,50-15">SK Hynix implemented 10-year 10%-of-operating-profit sharing agreement with initial bonuses ~$100k per person; Samsung refuses to institutionalize formula.</cite> <cite index="50-16,50-17">Rare migration direction—SK historically lagged Samsung—but bonus structure changed flow.</cite> Talent drain compounds Samsung execution risk in HBM ramp.

news_pulse.headline: Morgan Stanley no longer expects HBM3E price decline; China H200 demand adds ~$3bn incremental
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="9-1,9-8">MS reversed HBM3E decline view citing China H200 chip approval driving incremental demand; raised SK Hynix to ₩840k (29% upside).</cite> <cite index="9-6,9-7">2026/27 EPS lifted 56%/63%; DRAM +62% and NAND +75% in 2026 vs. prior forecasts.</cite> <cite index="9-3">Tightening supply across commodity and legacy HBM3E colliding with AI demand sets stage for steep increases.</cite>

brief.derivatives_signal: No ADR or futures data in payload; KOSPI vol elevated. <cite index="42-1,42-17">KOSPI rebounded to 7,516 (+0.31%) after sell-side sidecar trigger dropped index to 7,140 intraday; foreigners sold 9th consecutive session, dumping ~₩30tr this month.</cite> <cite index="42-19,42-20">Second time in 2026 sidecars activated two consecutive sessions (prior: March 3-4 post-Iran war outbreak).</cite> Implied vol spike suggests hedge demand. Watch for SK Hynix call skew expansion if ₩2m psychological level breaks; Samsung put volume likely elevated pre-strike. OTC Samsung ADR (SSNLF) and SK Hynix (HXSCL) offer offshore hedges but liquidity thin—recommend waiting for KRX close before positioning.
watch_for_next_3h: Samsung-union dialogue leaks or court injunction ruling on strike (expected 'any day' per sources); any delay past May 21 = immediate Samsung relief rally
KOSPI foreign flow reversal or ₩2m psychological break for SK Hynix—could trigger momentum cascade given 9-session foreign selling streak just ended
Hyperscaler earnings call transcripts for incremental CoWoS/HBM allocation commentary or 2H capex guidance revisions (Microsoft/Alphabet particularly)
TrendForce/DRAMeXchange May 18 spot price updates for DDR5/HBM3E; any further upward revision to Q3 contract forecasts confirms no relief scenario
Samsung HBM4 customer announcements (Nvidia Rubin, Broadcom, AWS Trainium) to offset strike noise and clarify vs. SK Hynix competitive positioning
